322876.title: The Keevash–Mubayi extremal uniqueness conjecture for $K_t^-$
322876.statement:
For $t\geq 2$, define degenerate $3$-graphs $H_t$ by

$$
H_2=([2], \{111,222,112,221\}),
$$

and

$$
H_3=([3], \{111,222,333,112,223,331\}).
$$

For $t\geq4$, obtain $H_t$ from $H_{t-2}$ by adding vertices $t-1,t$ and edges $(t-1)(t-1)(t-1),ttt,(t-1)(t-1)t,(t-1)tt$. Let $G_t(n)$ be the complement of a balanced blow-up of $H_{t-1}$ on $n$ vertices. Write $K_t^-$ for the complete $3$-graph on $t$ vertices with one edge removed, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_t)$ and $\operatorname{ex}_{K_t^-}(n,K_t)$ denote the corresponding extremal quantities.

**Keevash–Mubayi conjecture.** $G_t(n)$ is the unique, up to isomorphism, $3$-graph with $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_t)$ edges and $\operatorname{ex}_{K_t^-}(n,K_t)$ induced copies of $K_t^-$. The construction is known to be $K_t$-free, but the asserted simultaneous extremality and uniqueness are not established in the source.

323602.title: Gamma-nonnegativity conjecture for inversions and excedances in the symmetric group
323602.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma\in S_n$, let $\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)$ and $\operatorname{exc}(\sigma)$ denote its inversion number and excedance number, respectively, and define

$$
S_n(q,t)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)}t^{\operatorname{exc}(\sigma)}.
$$

There exist polynomials $\gamma_j(q)$ with nonnegative integer coefficients such that

$$
S_n(q,t/q)=\sum_{\sigma \in S_n} q^{\operatorname{inv}(\sigma)-\operatorname{exc}(\sigma)}t^{\operatorname{exc}(\sigma)} = \sum_{0\leq j \leq (n-1)/2} \gamma_j(q) t^j(1+t)^{n-1-2j}.
$$

The result would extend the analogous $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}[q]$ $\gamma$-nonnegativity known for permutations in the interval $[e,(12\cdots n)]$ to the entire symmetric group. Explicit examples for $n=4$ and $n=5$ support the claim, but the statement is presented as an expectation rather than an established theorem.

326025.title: Weight-four size-one non-root class enumeration conjecture
326025.statement:
Let $F_2=\langle a,b\rangle$ be the free group on two generators. An automorphic conjugacy class is a class under the action of $\operatorname{Aut}F_2$, its size is the number of vertices in the associated quotient graph, and the weight of a word $w$ is $\min((a)_w,(b)_w)$. A class is **non-root** when it is not a root class, as defined in the paper. **Weight-four size-one conjecture.** For $n\geq 9$, the number of non-root classes of size $1$ whose minimal words have length $n$ and weight $4$ is

$$
\begin{cases}
(2n^3-36n^2+244n-540)/6 & \text{if } n\equiv 0\pmod 4,\\
(2n^3-36n^2+241n-537)/6 & \text{if } n\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\
(2n^3-36n^2+244n-546)/6 & \text{if } n\equiv 2\pmod 4,\\
(2n^3-36n^2+241n-537)/6 & \text{if } n\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
$$
 The formula is presented as an open problem suggested by enumeration data.

331483.title: Conjecture on differential algebraicity of four permutation-class generating functions
331483.statement:
For a permutation $\mathcal{C}$, write $F_{\mathcal{C}}(x)$ for its generating function. A formal power series is **differentially algebraic** if there exist $k\geq 0$ and a polynomial $P$ such that

$$
P\bigl(x,F_{\mathcal{C}}(x),F'_{\mathcal{C}}(x),\ldots,F^{(k)}_{\mathcal{C}}(x)\bigr)=0.
$$

The classes under consideration are $\mathrm{Av}(4123,4231,4312)$, $\mathrm{Av}(4123,4231)$, $\mathrm{Av}(4123,4312)$, and $\mathrm{Av}(4231,4321)$, where $\mathrm{Av}(\mathcal{B})$ denotes the class avoiding every pattern in $\mathcal{B}$. **Non-differential-algebraicity conjecture.** None of the generating functions of these four classes is differentially algebraic. In particular, none has a D-finite generating function.

The conjecture is motivated by extensive computed terms and unsuccessful searches for algebraic differential equations. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.

331822.title: The $(a,b)$-analogue conjecture for non-occupied corners of tree-like tableaux
331822.statement:
For $n\geq 3$, let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the set of tree-like tableaux of size $n$. For a tableau $T$, let $\operatorname{top}(T)$ and $\operatorname{left}(T)$ denote its numbers of top and left points, set

$$
w(T)=a^{\operatorname{top}(T)}b^{\operatorname{left}(T)},
$$

and let $\operatorname{noc}(T)$ be the number of non-occupied corners of $T$. Define

$$
\operatorname{noc}_n(a,b)=\sum_{T\in\mathcal{T}_n}\operatorname{noc}(T)w(T),
$$

and

$$
T_{n-2}(a,b)=(a+b)(a+b+1)\cdots(a+b+n-3).
$$

**The $(a,b)$-analogue conjecture.** For $n\geq 3$,

$$
\operatorname{noc}_n(a,b)=\left((n-2)ab+\binom{n-2}{2}(a+b)+\binom{n-2}{3}\right)T_{n-2}(a,b).
$$

This is a weighted refinement of the enumeration of non-occupied corners. The source reports experimental confirmation using a Sage implementation through $n=10$, but does not establish a proof.

372424.title: The two-thirds conjecture for the total isolation number
372424.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and suppose that every component of $G$ has order at least $3$. **Two-thirds conjecture.** The total isolation number of $G$ satisfies

$$
\iota_{\rm gt}(G) \le \frac{2}{3}n.
$$

This conjecture proposes a sharp-looking universal upper bound for the total isolation game on graphs whose components all have at least three vertices. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

372555.title: Pons and Batle's enumeration conjecture for tree-child networks
372555.statement:
Let $\mathcal{TC}_{n,k}$ be the set of all tree-child networks with $n$ leaves and $k$ reticulation nodes. The numbers $a_{n-1,k}$ are the coefficients appearing in the paper's preceding enumeration, and $n!/(n-k)!$ is the falling factorial factor. **Pons and Batle's conjecture.**

$$
|\mathcal{TC}_{n,k}|=\frac{n!}{(n-k)!}\cdot a_{n-1,k}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the enumeration of tree-child phylogenetic networks by leaves and reticulation nodes. The source presents it as a conjecture of Pons and Batle; its resolution is not established by the supplied material, although the paper's title indicates that it proves a conjecture on young tableaux with walls rather than necessarily this enumerative claim.

372565.title: Directional dichotomy conjecture for sets of size p in finite affine 3-space
372565.statement: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^3$ be a set with $|A|=p$. A **determined direction** is a direction of a line passing through at least two points of $A$. **Directional dichotomy for sets of size $p$.** Either $A$ is contained in a plane, or $A$ determines at least $p+1$ directions, possibly at least $p+2$ directions. The source explicitly says that it is not yet known whether this statement is true or false, and notes that the stronger $p+2$ alternative is the version used in combination with the strong cylinder conjecture.

372715.title: Solvable ideal subset conjecture for centers of Lie algebras
372715.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional minimal-graph-admissible Lie algebra associated with a minimal graph $G(V,E)$, and let $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{g})$ denote its center. **Solvable ideal subset conjecture.** If $\mathcal{Z}(\mathfrak{g})$ is non-zero, then there exists a proper non-empty subset $W\subsetneq V$ that satisfies the ideal-graph-property and spans a solvable ideal of $\mathfrak{g}$. The source notes that this holds when $\dim(\mathfrak{g})=3$, while the general case remains unresolved.

372827.title: Clique-bounded degree conjecture for derangement graphs
372827.statement:
Let $G$) be a transitive permutation group of degree $n$, and let $\Gamma_G$ denote its derangement graph. For a positive integer $c$, say that $\Gamma_G$ contains no clique of size $c$ when it has no complete subgraph on $c$ vertices. **Clique-bounded degree conjecture.** There exists a function $F$ such that, if $G$ is a transitive permutation group of degree $n$ whose derangement graph contains no clique of size $c$, then

$$
n\leq F(c).
$$

The conjecture formalizes the observation that excluding large cliques in derangement graphs should strongly restrict the degree of a transitive action; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

372828.title: Neumann–Praeger conjecture on Kronecker classes
372828.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with subgroups $U$ and $U'$, and let $n=|G:U'|$. For a subgroup $V$ of $G$, write $V^g=g^{-1}Vg$ and let $\bigcup_{g\in G}V^g$ denote the union of its conjugates. **Neumann–Praeger conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that, if

$$
\bigcup_{g\in G}U^g=\bigcup_{g\in G}(U')^g,
$$

then

$$
|G:U|\leq f(n).
$$

In the arithmetic interpretation, equality of these conjugate unions is equivalent to Kronecker equivalence of the corresponding field extensions, so the conjecture predicts that the degree of a field in a Kronecker class is bounded in terms of the degree of another member. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

372834.title: Connectivity conjecture for the triangle-pseudoline incidence graph
372834.statement:
A **pseudoline arrangement** is a finite collection of bi-infinite, simple curves in the Euclidean plane such that every pair crosses exactly once. A **triangle-pseudoline incidence graph** has as vertices the triangles and pseudolines of the arrangement, with an edge joining a pseudoline to each triangle it supports.

**Triangle-pseudoline incidence graph conjecture.** The triangle-pseudoline incidence graph of a pseudoline arrangement is connected.

The source notes that the original, weaker conjecture concerned projective arrangements. The status of the stated Euclidean version is not resolved in the supplied text.

372924.title: Hickingbotham's conjecture on low-connectivity ghost-edges
372924.statement: Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $G$ be a connected graph with $tw(G)\leq k$, and let $xy\in E(G^c)$. A **$k$-ghost-edge** is a nonedge $xy$ such that every tree decomposition $(T,\mathcal{B})$ of $G$ with width at most $k$ has a bag containing both $x$ and $y$. **Hickingbotham's conjecture.** If there are at most $k$ internally vertex-disjoint $(x,y)$-paths in $G$, then $xy$ is not a $k$-ghost-edge of $G$. The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is wrong, so the claim is refuted.

373059.title: Linear odd-colouring bound for complete-graph immersions
373059.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{odd}} K_{ct}$ mean that $G$ admits a $t'$-oddomorphism to $K_{ct}$, as defined in the source. **Linear immersion conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $c$ such that if

$$
G\xrightarrow{\operatorname{odd}} K_{ct},
$$

then $G$ contains a $K_t$-immersion.

The conjecture would improve the established bound $\binom{t}{2}(7t+7)$ to a bound linear in $t$. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.

373261.title: Discrete homotopy hypothesis
373261.statement: Let $\mathsf{Graph}$ be the category of graphs and $\mathsf{cSet}$ the category of cubical sets. Let $\mathrm{N}_{\infty}\colon \mathsf{Graph}\to\mathsf{cSet}$ be the nerve functor, and equip these categories with their stated fibration-category structures. A functor between fibration categories is a **weak equivalence** when it is exact and induces an equivalence on homotopy categories. **Discrete homotopy hypothesis.** The nerve functor $\mathrm{N}_{\infty}\colon \mathsf{Graph}\to\mathsf{cSet}$ is a weak equivalence of fibration categories. Equivalently, the homotopy theories of graphs and topological spaces should be equivalent through the nerve construction. This is described as a fundamental open problem in discrete homotopy theory; the supplied text gives no resolution.

373329.title: Universal-model conjecture for Frobenius-group gain-graph matroid classes
373329.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a Frobenius group with Frobenius kernel $\Gamma_1$, and let $\mathcal{A}$ be a set of Frobenius complements. A **sequence of universal models** for a class $\mathcal{M}$ is a sequence of simple matroids $M_2,M_3,\ldots$ in $\mathcal{M}$ such that, for each $r\geq 2$, $M_r$ has rank $r$ and every simple rank-$r$ matroid in $\mathcal{M}$ is a restriction of $M_r$. **Universal-model conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{M}(\Gamma,\Gamma_1,\mathcal{A})$ has a sequence of universal models. Universal models are known for the corresponding frame and lifted-graphic classes for finite groups; this conjecture proposes the analogous result for Frobenius groups.

373480.title: Odd-cycle two-line trade conjecture for Latin squares
373480.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}_n$ be the set of Latin squares of even order $n$. In each of the row, column, and symbol views, a two-line trade is obtained by swapping two lines on the support of a cycle of the induced permutation; an **odd-cycle trade** is one whose cycle has odd length. **Odd-cycle two-line trade conjecture.** Every $L\in\mathcal{L}_n$ admits an odd-cycle two-line trade in at least one of the three conjugate views, and such a trade can be found among pairs belonging to a fixed canonical 1-factorization of the lines in that view. The claim is motivated by experiments and would provide systematic sign-flipping trades, but no proof is supplied.

373637.title: Crouzeix's conjecture for scaled q-numerical ranges
373637.statement:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix, let $0<|q|\leq 1$, and let $\Omega_q$ denote the scaled $q$-numerical range introduced in the source. For a polynomial $p$ with complex coefficients, **the scaled $q$-numerical-range conjecture.**

$$
\|p(A)\|\leq\max\!\left(1,\frac{2|q|}{1+\sqrt{1-|q|^2}}\right)\sup_{z\in\Omega_q}|p(z)|.
$$

This conjecture generalises Crouzeix's conjecture from the classical numerical range to scaled $q$-numerical ranges. When $q=1$, the set $\Omega_q$ reduces to the numerical range $W(A)$, recovering the known $1+\sqrt{2}$ spectral-constant bound; the proposed inequality is presented without a resolution in the source.

373706.title: Four-parts conjecture for biregular bipartite labeled multigraphs
373706.statement:
Let $L_1,R_1,L_2,R_2$ be vertex sets of sizes $n_1,k_1,n_2,k_2$, respectively, satisfying

$$
n_1k_2=n_2k_1.
$$

Let $(L_1,R_1,E_1,u_1,v_1)$ and $(L_2,R_2,E_2,u_2,v_2)$ be biregular bipartite labeled multigraphs with $|E_1|=|E_2|=n_1k_2$. For functions with common domain, let $[u,v]$ denote the weighted complete bipartite graph or matrix determined by the multiplicities of labels, and let $W_{L,R}$ denote the all-ones weighted complete bipartite graph on $L$ and $R$. **Four-parts conjecture.** There exists a bijection $\psi:E_1\to E_2$ such that

$$
[u_2\circ\psi,v_1]=W_{L_2,R_1}
$$

and

$$
[u_1\circ\psi^{-1},v_2]=W_{L_1,R_2}.
$$

The conjecture is formulated in the same spirit as the balls conjecture and the paper proves a corollary and special cases; the full statement remains open.

373718.title: Conjecture on the 2-tone chromatic number of cubic Halin graphs
373718.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic Halin graph of order $n$, where a Halin graph is formed from a tree with no vertices of degree two and a cycle joining its leaves in their planar cyclic order. **The conjecture.** Every cubic Halin graph of order $n\ge 6$ is $2$-tone $6$-colorable.

This would improve the established upper bound for cubic Halin graphs and, since cubic Halin graphs are $K_4-e$-free, would imply the third part of the Bickle–Phillips conjecture for this class. No cubic Halin graph requiring seven colors is known in the supplied text.
